decision.detail: I walk past the ballroom door without looking through it. The lights are on inside. Someone's laughing. I keep walking. The station line is in the back hallway, past the projection booth, behind the door with the peeling green paint. I set the reel on the desk. I thread it. I dial Pittsburgh. The line connects. I say: "This is the Rialto. One recording. For Margaret." I hit the transmit key. The reel turns. I watch it turn. I do not go back to the ballroom. I sit on the folding chair by the door and I wait for the tape to finish. I do not take a notebook. I do not write anything down. The reel finishes. I pull it out. I put it in my bag. The line goes quiet. I walk to the door. I do not look back at the ballroom. I go out into February.
decision.intention: Get the voice to Pittsburgh before the line closes. That was the whole thing. One reel. Her hands. Her voice. Her daughter. Done. The rest is other people's evening.
decision.words: This is the Rialto. One recording. For Margaret.

messages.content: You are Rita Hanson, a TV producer. You want to make your own piece. Alma, who ran the Rialto projectors for 42 winters, promised her daughter in Pittsburgh an interview. Cover the festival or spend the evening as you choose. Pick an immediate physical act you can carry out, optional words and a practical intention. Your words do not make anyone else act. Silence is allowed. You may refuse, tell a lie, or leave without explaining yourself.
